notes.decision: Translated as 'Of the Chapters' — the genitive ⲛ̄- prefix indicates this is a running header marker ('[the book/text] of the Chapters') rather than an individual chapter title. Standard Manichaean codex header.

Treating the editor's single-letter restoration [ⲙ] at the start of line 1 as part of certain text. The remainder of ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϭ ('Greatness,' = ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ in Lyc glossary) is preserved; the ⲙ is securely restored from context. Single-letter restorations completing obvious words are treated as certain throughout this page per pragmatic editorial choice. The word likely continues from a phrase on the prior page (e.g., 'the Son of/the Power of/the Ambassador of [the] Greatness'); the visible noun functions as predicate genitive of an unnamed subject — the Ambassador per the chapter context (line 6).

The word ⲙⲛⲧⲁϣⲗⲣⲉ (split across lines 2-3) is an unidentified abstract noun. Possibilities include: (a) a Lyc form related to ϣⲗⲏⲗ 'pray' giving 'prayer-state' (fitting the chapter's prayer theme); (b) a form related to ϣⲏⲣⲉ 'child' giving 'sonship/childhood' (fitting the works of the Five Sons); (c) a privative ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲁⲧ-X. Translated as '[X]hood' pending parallels.

ⲡⲓⲉⲙⲛⲧⲉ = 'this Hades/Underworld' (= ⲁⲙⲛⲧⲉ, Lyc with prosthetic ⲉ-). In Manichaean cosmology this names the lower realm of death and oppression where the soul is bound. ϣⲁⲭⲍ is a qualitative of uncertain root — possibly related to ϣⲱϫⲉ 'destroy/burn' or ϣⲱϫϩ 'be afflicted' — giving 'harsh/scorching/painful.' The pairing with 'oppression' (ⲑⲗⲓⲃⲉ) and 'lower side' (ⲡⲥⲁⲙⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ) supports a sense of harshness or scorching.

Qualitative of ⲙⲟⲩϫⲧ̄/ⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄ 'mingle, be kneaded together' (in glossary) — the soul 'while being mingled in them' (the fleshes of death). Standard Manichaean cosmogonic-anthropological vocabulary for the entanglement of light-substance with dark matter.

From ⲟⲩⲱⲥⲧⲛ̄ 'be wide, spread' (cf. ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'wide/broad' in glossary). Causative: 'he made (her) wide,' 'he gave wideness/relief.' Soteriological liberation expressed spatially as the giving-of-room.

Apparent variant of ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'purpose of heart' (in glossary) — the third instance in this passage's enumeration (lines 12-13 ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛ̄|ⲍⲏⲧ; line 16 ⲡⲱⲛⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ). The ⲛ̄ may be a scribal slip or a Lyc variant stem. Translated identically as 'purpose of heart.' Could alternatively reflect ⲡⲱⲛⲕ 'scoop/draw out' (ⲡⲱⲛⲕ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ = 'drawing-forth of heart'), but consistency with lines 12-13 favors 'purpose.'

Lexeme not securely identifiable. The form ⲁϥⲡ̄ⲟⲇⲟ (with possible word-internal break ⲡ̄ ⲟⲇⲟ in transcription) is likely a verb of motion/conveyance. Possibilities: (a) Greek προοδέω/πρόοδος 'advance, lead forth'; (b) Coptic ⲡⲱⲱⲇⲉ 'leap, pass over'; (c) Greek πηδάω 'leap'; (d) ⲡⲱⲧ 'run' in some extended form. The collocation ⲍⲓ ⲍⲟⲩⲓⲧ 'as foremost' and directional ⲁ-ⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ ⲧⲏⲣϥ 'to the whole body' supports a sense of leading-forth as guide. Translated 'led-forth as foremost' tentatively. Flagged as proposed term.

1sg perfect of ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲥ 'raise, awaken' (cf. ⲣⲉϩⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲥ 'the Awakener' in glossary) with 2sg.m suffix -ⲉⲧⲕ — 'I have raised you up forth.' Apostolic-soteriological speech: the Ambassador addresses the soul/disciple as having been raised. Per terminology guide, ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲥ-class verbs preserve vertical-soteriological semantics; rendered 'raised up forth.'
Circumstantial + ⲥⲱⲡⲥ̄ 'beseech, entreat' with 3sg.f object suffix -ⲥ̄ — 'beseeching her' (the prayer/the soul). The prayer is here treated as feminine, parallel to the soul (ϯⲩⲭⲏ).

Likely scribal/dialectal for ⲁⲗⲗⲁ ⲙⲁⲣⲛ̄ⲉⲓ 'but let us come' — concessive ⲁⲗⲗⲁ + 1pl jussive ⲙⲁⲣⲛ̄- + ⲉⲓ 'come.' Standard Coptic exhortation introducing a new section. The doubled ⲗ-onset and ⲣ for ⲙⲁⲣ may reflect Lyc orthographic features or scribal compression.
